question.prompt: Aaliyah rolls two standard \(6\)-sided dice. She notices that the product of the two numbers rolled is a multiple of \(6.\) Which of the following integers cannot be the sum of the two numbers?

solutions.explanation:
A sum is possible only if some pair of dice numbers gives that sum and has a product that is a multiple of \(6\).

For a sum of \(6\), the possible pairs, ignoring order, are
\[
(1,5),\quad (2,4),\quad (3,3).
\]
These include every pair: choosing the smaller number as \(1\), \(2\), or \(3\) determines the other number. Reversing a pair changes neither its sum nor its product. Their products are \(5\), \(8\), and \(9\), respectively, so none qualifies.

Each other listed sum does occur with a suitable product:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2+3&=5, &2\times3&=6,\\
1+6&=7, &1\times6&=6,\\
2+6&=8, &2\times6&=12,\\
3+6&=9, &3\times6&=18.
\end{aligned}
\]
All four products are multiples of \(6\). Therefore the sum that cannot occur is \(6\), choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
solutions.title: Check the possible pairs for each sum
